rules.halloween_dictionary: v1.1: sections 1–13 excluding Doll; sections 14–15 omitted

candidates.title: Panic at the Pumpkin Patch
candidates.artist_description: Holiday-horror metal/hyperpop project performed by Harrow Everbright and Vesper Snow; composition assistance disclosed in album credits.
candidates.match_reason: Title directly combines panic and pumpkin patch; lyrics reinforce supernatural and death themes.
candidates.lyric_summary: A pumpkin-patch nightmare satirizes viral panic, mass hysteria, witchcraft and an apocalyptic harvest. The chorus forecasts panic, and the lyrics turn pumpkins into predatory horrors.
candidates.lyric_excerpt: Tonight’s forecast: panic in the sky

candidates.title: Stinky Feet

candidates.match_reason: Exact “Stinky” in title; lyrics reference vampires, sacrifice, and hiding bodies in a macabre-comic context.
candidates.lyric_summary: An absurd pledge of devotion: the narrator imagines sacrifice, bodies hidden, vampirism and other grotesque scenarios, then circles back to the comic title.
candidates.lyric_excerpt: would you hide the bodies with me?

candidates.title: Haunted

candidates.lyric_summary: An eerie, waterlogged lament about being swept out to sea and begging for a rescuer. The supernatural mood is reinforced by the song’s repeated haunting motif.

candidates.title: Locked in a Haunted Attic (Alone) – Clownvis to the Rescue

candidates.lyric_excerpt: locked in a haunted attic alone

candidates.artist_description: Los Angeles rock band, with fantastical and unsettling narratives in published song lyrics.
candidates.match_reason: Lyrics describe tossing and turning during a grotesque supernatural shipboard nightmare.
candidates.lyric_summary: A disturbed, nightmare-like journey in which tossing and turning mixes with ominous violence and otherworldly dread. Published lyrics contain the prompt.

candidates.title: Toss/Turn
candidates.artist_description: Pittsburgh pop-punk group.
candidates.match_reason: Exact toss in the title; lyrics include a snake in a skull and a sickly sense of dread.
candidates.lyric_summary: Restless unease, guilt and sickness: the narrator speaks of something inside their skull, blood, spiraling thoughts and no apparent escape.
candidates.lyric_excerpt: There’s a snake in my skull

candidates.title: Flimsy Steve
candidates.artist_description: Chicago experimental songwriter/producer.
candidates.match_reason: Flimsy is exact in the title, but the occult tie is weak; project bio jokingly references a ghost and exorcism.
candidates.evidence: Title + artist profile only — low confidence
candidates.lyric_summary: The named figure Flimsy Steve is a weary traveler wrestling with identity and mental strain. The lyrics do not establish a convincing Halloween connection; this is a low-priority research lead.

candidates.title: Vampire lady
candidates.artist_description: German rock/reggae/punk/ska band active from 1996 to 2017.

candidates.lyric_summary: A barroom vampire encounter with a mysterious woman who drinks blood. Both the title and the narrative connect directly to the prompt and classic monster imagery.

candidates.title: Spooky (Without You)
candidates.artist_description: Alt-R&B project based in Columbia, South Carolina, led by vocalist/songwriter Desirée Richardson and a rotating cast of musicians.
candidates.match_reason: Published lyrics contain “hip, hip, hooray” during a gleefully sinister scene involving a séance, death, bones and confinement. Halloween tag is explicit.
candidates.evidence: Published lyrics + Halloween tag + song credits
candidates.lyric_summary: A gleefully eerie song about love, death and haunting, with a celebratory “hooray” that is part of the lyric. Séance and confinement imagery turn the celebration sinister.

candidates.title: Into the Woods
candidates.artist_description: Home-recorded Portland, Oregon musical project by Austin Rose.
candidates.match_reason: Published lyrics explicitly pair “Hooray” with a ghost, resurrection, demons, death and sleep paralysis.
candidates.lyric_summary: A spirited woodland horror story that combines a joyful “hooray” with ghosts, demons, resurrection and sleep-paralysis imagery. The contrast makes the lyric memorable.

candidates.title: Hooray for Horrorwood

candidates.notes: Bandcamp link not yet verified; external label page retained transparently.
candidates.lyric_summary: No verified published lyrics available for this recording; not eligible for the main lyric-first candidate list.

candidates.lyric_excerpt: I’m half human and half machine
